facts.fact_text: On 13 October 2008, the applicant applied to the Budapest Police Department for authorisation for a political demonstration in front of Parliament, in Kossuth Square.
Kossuth Square is a vast open area traditionally used for political demonstrations.
One of the declared objectives of the planned demonstration was commemoration of the revolution of 1956.
One of the declared objectives of the planned demonstration was commemoration of the tumultuous events in Budapest in 2006.
One of the declared objectives of the planned demonstration was to call attention to the perceived absence of legal certainty in Hungary.
The planned demonstration was scheduled for Friday, 17 October 2008.
On 15 October 2008, the Budapest Police Department forbade the applicant's planned demonstration.
The applicant applied for judicial review of the Budapest Police Department's decision forbidding the demonstration.
On 22 October 2008, the Budapest Regional Court dismissed the applicant's complaint against the Budapest Police Department's decision forbidding the demonstration.
The Budapest Police Department considered that 'gravely endangering' the functioning of Parliament was a legitimate ground for prohibiting the demonstration under section 8(1) of the Assembly Act.
The Budapest Police Department was of the view that the planned demonstration would 'gravely endanger' the functioning of Parliament.

The Budapest Police Department considered that participants physically impeding Members of Parliament from driving in and out of Parliament's car park would amount to restricting the Members of Parliament's freedom of movement.

The Budapest Police Department considered that participants physically impeding Members of Parliament from driving in and out of Parliament's car park would amount to inhibiting the functioning of the organ of the people's representation.

According to Parliament's official and public activity log available on the Internet, the only event taking place on 17 October 2008 in Parliament's building was a conference and open day organised by the Hungarian Alliance for Enhancing Female Careers under the title 'Employment – Equality of Chances – Competitiveness'.
According to Parliament's official and public activity log available on the Internet, no parliamentary session was scheduled for 17 October 2008.
On 14 October 2008, the Budapest Police Department proposed to the applicant that the planned demonstration be held in a secluded part of Kossuth Square, rather than its entirety.
The applicant refused the Budapest Police Department's suggestion to hold the demonstration in a secluded part of Kossuth Square.
The Budapest Police Department was of the view that the planned demonstration would 'gravely endanger' the functioning of Parliament.
The Budapest Police Department considered that amplified speeches and music belonging to the programme of the planned demonstration might disturb the Members of Parliament's work.
The Budapest Police Department estimated the number of participants in the planned demonstration at 150 to 200 persons.
The Budapest Police Department considered that participants in the planned demonstration might physically impede Members of Parliament from driving in and out of Parliament's car park.

The applicant submitted that another demonstration with an agenda identical to his, scheduled for Wednesday, 15 October 2008, had not been forbidden on exactly the same location as his planned demonstration.
The applicant submitted that the fact that the other demonstration on 15 October 2008 had not been forbidden showed discrimination against him and his planned event.
According to Parliament's official and public activity log available on the Internet, on 15 October 2008 five parliamentary commissions were in session.
The Budapest Regional Court endorsed in essence the Budapest Police Department's reasoning for forbidding the demonstration.
